sections.h2: What happens to a Montana tenant when the landlord sells the house?
sections.html:
The lease stays in place, and the buyer steps into the seller's position as landlord. Montana Code Annotated 70-26-102 gives a person who receives transferred real property on which rent is reserved the same remedies for rent, nonperformance of lease terms, waste or forfeiture that the seller had.

That rule is why a tenant cannot be removed simply because a sale is coming. A buyer who wants the house empty has to wait out the lease or use a termination route the law allows. A buyer who wants a rental can keep the tenant and the rent roll.

Montana also protects the seller once the sale is done. Under 70-24-304, a landlord who conveys the premises in a good faith sale to a bona fide purchaser is relieved of liability under the rental agreement and the Residential Landlord and Tenant Act for events occurring after written notice to the tenant of the conveyance. Unless otherwise agreed, the seller stays liable for all security recoverable by the tenant and for all prepaid rent.

In plain terms, send the tenant a written notice of the sale, and settle the deposit and any prepaid rent with the buyer at closing so the money follows the lease.

sections.h2: Which Montana laws govern a rental?
sections.html:
Most residential rentals fall under the Residential Landlord and Tenant Act of 1977, MCA Title 70, chapter 24, and the Residential Tenants' Security Deposits chapter, Title 70, chapter 25. The Montana courts website points landlords and tenants to those two laws, plus chapter 26 on landlord and tenant residential and commercial matters and the state's prohibited discriminatory practices statute in Title 49.

Chapter 25 applies to all rentals of dwellings subject to Title 70, chapter 24, or chapter 33, which covers mobile home lots. Federal fair housing law applies on top of the state rules.

The Montana Judicial Branch hosts a landlord handbook of 31 pages and a tenant handbook of 29 pages, along with forms, on its landlord and tenant page. Both sides can read them without paying anything.

sections.h2: How much notice does a landlord have to give to end a Montana tenancy?
sections.html:
It depends on the reason. For a month-to-month tenancy, either side may end it with at least 30 days' written notice under 70-24-441, and for week-to-week the notice is 7 days. For a breach by the tenant, 70-24-422 sets shorter and varied periods.

  • Unpaid rent: the tenant has 3 days after written notice of nonpayment and of the landlord's intent to terminate to pay.
  • Unauthorized pet: 3 days.
  • Unauthorized people living in the unit: 3 days.
  • Most other noncompliance: 14 days, and the lease does not end if the tenant fixes the problem before the date in the notice.
  • Same breach repeated within 6 months: at least 5 days' written notice.
  • Verbal abuse of the landlord, or damage or danger to the premises or neighbors: 3 days.

The statute says a landlord who uses the 30-day month-to-month notice is not bound by the breach rules in 70-24-422. Acceptance of full rent due waives a claimed breach only when the claimed breach is nonpayment, according to 70-24-423.

The notice must be in writing and specify the acts or omissions. Follow the statute closely when a sale is waiting on possession.

sections.h2: How does a Montana landlord evict, and where are the forms?
sections.html:
If the tenant does not leave after a valid notice, the landlord files an action for possession in court. The Montana courts site offers a Notice to Vacate, an Action for Possession packet for asking the court to evict, a Writ of Assistance form, and a letter for notifying a tenant of additional cleaning after move-out.

Under 70-24-427, once a rental agreement is terminated the landlord has a claim for possession, rent and damages. Under 70-24-422(5), a landlord may recover actual damages and seek an injunction for a tenant's noncompliance, and may recover treble damages if the noncompliance is purposeful, though not for early termination of the tenancy.

Montana does not allow a landlord to retaliate. Under 70-24-431, a landlord may not raise rent, cut services or threaten a possession action because the tenant complained to a housing-code agency, complained in writing about a violation, or joined a tenant organization. A landlord who tries to clear a house for a sale right after a repair complaint should expect that issue to come up.

The courts' Court Help Program, reached at (406) 841-2975, and the Montana Legal Services HelpLine at 1-800-666-6899 are listed by the Montana courts among legal help resources. The Court Help Program offers free assistance on common civil legal issues.

sections.h2: What deposit and entry rules apply while a sale is pending?
sections.html:
Showing the house is allowed, but entry rules still apply. The landlord must give at least 24 hours' notice to enter, except in an emergency or when it is impracticable, and may enter only at reasonable times. A seller with a photographer, appraiser or buyer's inspector scheduled should plan around that notice.

The deposit rules matter just as much. The statute 70-25-102 applies chapter 25 to covered dwellings, and 70-25-206 requires a statement of the condition of the premises at the start of a lease. At the end of a tenancy the landlord has 30 days to deliver the written list of charges with any balance, or 10 days where nothing is owed. A landlord who misses the list forfeits the right to withhold for damage or cleaning.

  • Get the deposit amount and the move-in condition statement into the sale file.
  • Decide in the purchase contract whether the deposit transfers to the buyer or is credited at closing.
  • Keep copies of the written notice of conveyance you send the tenant.

sections.h2: Does a tenant change how a rental sells for cash?
sections.html:
Yes, because the occupancy, rent level and lease end date set the price a buyer can pay. A tenant-occupied house is bought as an income property or as a future empty house, and the offer reflects which.

Cash buyers can take the house with the tenant in place, so you do not have to rush a move-out or pay for repairs before closing. If you would rather deliver the house empty, the notice periods above are the lawful way to do it, and a month-to-month tenancy needs the 30 days.

The tax side can help a seller explain the numbers. The Montana Department of Revenue Long-Term Rental Reduced Rate applies to a property rented for 28 or more days at a time, for at least seven months of the year, as the tenant's residence. Short-term rentals, such as vacation rentals, and second homes fall under the flat 1.90% rate for 2026, so rental use changes what a new owner pays in tax.

Cash Home Buyers can review a Montana rental and give a written cash offer. We give general information here, not legal advice, so use the court forms or an attorney for any notice you plan to serve.

faqs.q: Can a Montana landlord end a lease early because the house is being sold?
faqs.a: Not by itself. A buyer takes over the landlord's rights under the existing lease, so the tenant stays until the lease ends or a lawful termination applies. For a month-to-month tenancy, either side can end it with at least 30 days' written notice under MCA 70-24-441.

faqs.q: How many days does a Montana tenant have to pay rent after a notice?
faqs.a: Three days after written notice of nonpayment and of the landlord's intention to terminate the agreement. If the tenant does not pay within that period, the landlord may terminate and the tenant must vacate under MCA 70-24-422.

faqs.q: Who keeps the security deposit when a Montana rental sells?
faqs.a: The selling landlord stays liable to the tenant for security recoverable under Title 70, chapter 25, and for prepaid rent, unless otherwise agreed. Sellers usually settle that with the buyer at closing so the funds follow the lease.

faqs.q: How much notice must a Montana landlord give before entering a rental?
faqs.a: At least 24 hours, except in an emergency or when notice is impracticable, and entry must be at reasonable times under MCA 70-24-312.

faqs.q: Where can a Montana landlord find eviction forms?
faqs.a: The Montana Judicial Branch landlord and tenant page provides a Notice to Vacate, an Action for Possession packet, a Writ of Assistance form and a landlord handbook.
